thread:
eva: Heads-up — opened a quick thread about telemetry-brokerage + fastpath fallback for canaries. Wanted to capture the operator handoff heuristics we discussed in the meeting earlier.

sam: nice. can you sketch the flow? is this a new component or glue between observer and decision-plane?

liam: +1 on diagram pls. my main worry: extra hop adds latency to critical degrade decisions.

eva: it's a thin "telemetry-broker" layer. idea: observers (probes, clients, runtime meters) publish dense signals to the broker, which normalizes, dedups and emits downsampled summaries to the decision plane. broker also holds a short-lived fastpath state cache for immediate fallbacks.

priya: sounds promising. how is this different from existing observer aggregator?

eva: two differences: 1) brokerage is policy-aware (applies sampling/weighting based on rollout cohort) so can keep per-cohort SLOs separate. 2) fastpath cache — an in-memory local cache that can trigger an immediate fallback without waiting for round-trip to central decisioning when probe confidence > threshold.

sam: define "probe confidence"?

liam: propose simple score: weighted combination of error-rate spike, latency p95 delta, and a model-quality signal if available. score in [0,1]. broker exposes config: "fastpath_threshold": 0.85 by default.

priya: can we see a config snippet?

eva: sure:

```
# broker policy example
fastpath_enabled: true
fastpath_threshold: 0.85
fastpath_ttl_secs: 10
cohort_weights:
  canary: 1.2
  baseline: 1.0
summary_interval_ms: 200
```

liam: ttl=10s seems short — but good for preventing flapping. how do we avoid false positives from noisy probes?

eva: broker smooths signals with an exponential window and requires at least 3 distinct probe sources crossing threshold within window before fastpath triggers. also we have a short cooldown per-cohort.

sam: operator handoff: what happens when fastpath fires but operator wants to override? do we surface in console + slack?

priya: we should include an operator breakglass that can pin route to baseline or pause rollouts. broker will emit a "fastpath.action" event that the control plane can block on if operator intervention requested.

eva: proposed run: fastpath triggers -> broker publishes event -> control plane applies local fallback immediately (optimistic) while marking action "pending-operator". if operator clicks "hold" in console within 30s, we either keep fallback or roll forward depending on manual decision. fallback is reversible.

liam: optimistic apply worries me. can we make it conditional: if fallback cost (latency/cost delta) < X then optimistic, else require central ack?

sam: yes, include a policy: "fastpath_mode: optimistic|gate". default optimistic for low-risk endpoints, gate for high-risk tenants.

priya: telemetry guarantees: broker must sign events with causal ids so decision-plane and runbook can correlate. also we need idempotency keys for repeated fastpath attempts.

runbot: deploy-broker v0.2 -> rollout to staging cluster tonight :rocket: (logs at https://ci.internal/reports/BR-321)

eva: good. one more nuance: local cache consistency during split traffic. If model variant A is warmed in a region and we fallback to baseline model B, broker must record variant affinity TTL to avoid routing churn. default affinity_ttl: 60s.

liam: i want a small state machine documented for operator handoff:

- FASTPATH_TRIGGERED -> OPTIMISTIC_APPLY -> OPERATOR_PENDING -> (OPERATOR_APPROVE | OPERATOR_REVERT | TIMEOUT)
- If TIMEOUT and no operator action -> revert to central policy (by default revert unless policy says persist)

priya: add an audit event for every transition. must include: cohort_id, variant_ids, trigger_score, probe_ids, operator_id(optional).

sam: testing plan: chaos tests that drop probes, synthetic spike generator, and a simulated slow decision-plane to ensure fastpath doesn't oscillate. also e2e with console breakglass UX.

eva: action items:
- sam: prototype broker normalization + fastpath cache (POC 2 days)
- priya: write operator handoff API + console hooks (PR for UI flows)
- liam: design state-machine + audit schema (doc)
- eva: add canary cohort weighting proposals to RFC v2

sam: cool. ping me if you need infra for memstore.

priya: will stub Slack integration: post when FASTPATH_TRIGGERED with one-click acknowledge.

eva: thanks — I'll drop a short diagram in the RFC and link this thread. :thumbsup:
